<html lang="ko">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>어구독 예비고1 WEEK 01</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/orioncactus/pretendard@v1.3.9/dist/web/static/pretendard.min.css">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:wght@200;300;400;500;600&family=Source+Serif+4:ital,wght@0,400;0,600;0,700;1,400&family=Nanum+Pen+Script&family=Inter:wght@400;600;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<style>
@page { size: A4; margin: 0; }

html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; background: #fff; }
body { word-break: keep-all; overflow-wrap: break-word; font-family: Pretendard, sans-serif; color: #17181c; font-size: 9.2pt; line-height: 1.5; -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact; print-color-adjust: exact; }
:root { --ink: #121a33; --navy: #1b2a57; --acc: #ff5a1f; --acc2: #ffb800; --hl: #ffe45c; --gray: #6a6d76; --rule: #d3d6dd; --cream: #fbf7ef; }
.page { width: 210mm; height: 297mm; padding: 12mm 14mm 15mm; position: relative; overflow: hidden; break-after: page; }
.page:last-child { break-after: auto; }
.en { font-family: Inter, Pretendard, sans-serif; font-size: 9.2pt; line-height: 1.62; letter-spacing: -0.005em; }
.disp { font-family: "Black Han Sans", Pretendard, sans-serif; font-weight: 400; }
.hl { background: linear-gradient(transparent 58%, var(--hl) 58%); }
.tip { font-family: "Nanum Pen Script", cursive; font-weight: 400; color: var(--acc); font-size: 15pt; line-height: 1.15; }
.tip b { font-family: Inter, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 7pt; letter-spacing: 0.12em; color: #fff; background: var(--acc); padding: 0.6mm 1.6mm; border-radius: 1mm; margin-right: 2mm; vertical-align: 1.5pt; }
/* running head */
.run { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 7.4pt; color: var(--gray); margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.run .brand { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.run .brand i { font-style: normal; color: var(--acc); }
.foot { position: absolute; left: 14mm; right: 14mm; bottom: 8mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); }
.foot .pg { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
/* part head */
.part { display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: end; column-gap: 4mm; padding-bottom: 2.5mm; border-bottom: 2pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.part .no { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 44pt; line-height: 0.8; color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1.4pt var(--navy); }
.part .no.fill { color: var(--acc); -webkit-text-stroke: 0; }
.part .ttl .e { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 18pt; color: var(--navy); line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.01em; }
.part .ttl .k { font-size: 9.6pt; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-top: 1.2mm; }
.part .meta { text-align: right; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); line-height: 1.35; }
.part .meta .time { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; color: var(--acc); font-size: 13pt; display: block; }
.qr { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 13mm; height: 13mm; border: 0.8pt dashed #9aa0ab; font-size: 5.8pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: center; line-height: 1.2; margin-left: 3mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.part .meta-wrap { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; }
h3.pt { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 2.5mm; margin: 4.5mm 0 2mm; font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 800; color: var(--ink); }
h3.pt .n { font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: #fff; background: var(--navy); font-size: 7.6pt; padding: 0.6mm 1.8mm; letter-spacing: 0.08em; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
h3.pt small { font-weight: 500; color: var(--gray); font-size: 8pt; margin-left: auto; }
.lead { margin: 0 0 3mm; color: #33363d; }
/* 판서노트 표 */
table.note { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.9pt; }
table.note th { text-align: left; font-size: 8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.2mm 1.5mm; }
table.note td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.9mm 1.5mm; vertical-align: top; }
table.note td.k { font-weight: 700; width: 46mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 30mm; }
.blank { display: inline-block; min-width: 18mm; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); text-align: center; color: transparent; }
.ex div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.ok { color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; }
.chk { display: inline-block; width: 3.1mm; height: 3.1mm; border: 0.7pt solid #7d828c; vertical-align: -0.4mm; margin: 0 0.6mm; }
ol.q { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; counter-reset: q; }
ol.q > li { counter-increment: q; position: relative; padding-left: 7.5mm; margin-bottom: 2.1mm; }
ol.q > li::before { content: counter(q); position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.3mm; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; color: var(--navy); font-size: 9pt; }
.cols2 { column-count: 2; column-gap: 7mm; column-rule: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
.cols2 > * { break-inside: avoid; }
.c { font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap; }
.ox { float: right; color: var(--gray); font-family: Inter; font-weight: 600; font-size: 8pt; }
.wl { display: inline-block; border-bottom: 0.6pt solid #8b9099; min-width: 30mm; height: 4mm; vertical-align: bottom; }
.line { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid #b9bdc5; height: 7mm; }
.passage { margin: 1mm 0 2.5mm; text-align: justify; }
.src { font-family: Inter; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--acc); font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.qhead { font-weight: 800; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; font-size: 9.2pt; }
.qhead .src { margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.opts { font-size: 8.6pt; margin: 0 0 1mm; }
.opts div { margin: 0.4mm 0; }
.gloss { font-size: 7.2pt; color: var(--gray); text-align: right; margin-top: -1mm; margin-bottom: 1.5mm; }
.rd { break-inside: avoid; margin-bottom: 5mm; }
.pat { margin-bottom: 4.6mm; }
.pat .f { display: inline-block; font-family: Inter; font-weight: 800; font-size: 9pt; color: #fff; background: var(--ink); padding: 0.6mm 2.2mm; margin-right: 2mm; }
.pat .fk { font-weight: 700; }
.pat .s { margin: 1.6mm 0 0 0; }
.cond { font-size: 8.4pt; color: #333; border-top: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.4mm 0; margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; }
.cond b { color: var(--navy); margin-right: 2mm; }
.bogi { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; padding: 1.6mm 0; border-top: 1pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); margin: 1.2mm 0 2mm; word-spacing: 1.5mm; }
.tr { margin-bottom: 2.4mm; }
.tr .no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--navy); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 8.6pt; }
/* voca */
table.voc { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.voc td { padding: 1.35mm 1mm; border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); }
table.voc td.n { width: 6mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: #a3a8b2; font-size: 7pt; }
table.voc td.w { font-family: Inter; font-weight: 700; width: 33mm; }
table.voc td.b { width: 30mm; }
/* plan */
table.grid { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.7pt; }
table.grid th { text-align: left; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); font-weight: 600; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding: 1.4mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td { border-bottom: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 2mm 1.5mm; }
table.grid td.no { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); width: 10mm; }
.score { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.2fr 1fr 1fr 1.4fr; border-top: 2pt solid var(--ink); border-bottom: 0.6pt solid var(--ink); margin-bottom: 4mm; }
.score div { padding: 1.6mm 2.5mm; border-right: 0.5pt solid var(--rule); height: 13mm; font-size: 7.8pt; color: var(--gray); }
.score div:last-child { border-right: 0; }
.score b { display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.2pt; }
.key h4 { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 8.6pt; color: var(--navy); margin: 3.4mm 0 1.2mm; letter-spacing: 0.04em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: 0.8mm; }
.key h4 span { font-family: Pretendard; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin-left: 1.5mm; }
.key .row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.6mm 4.5mm; font-size: 8.4pt; }
.key .row b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 8.2pt; margin: 0.6mm 0; }
.key .ls b { font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--acc); margin-right: 1.5mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
/* cover */
.cover { padding: 0; color: #fff; background: radial-gradient(120% 80% at 75% 35%, #2d3f86 0%, #17214a 45%, #0b1024 100%); }
.cover svg.art { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; width: 210mm; height: 297mm; }
.cover .top { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; top: 15mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; font-size: 8.6pt; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
.cover .pill { border: 0.8pt solid rgba(255,255,255,.75); border-radius: 10mm; padding: 1mm 3.2mm; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .series { opacity: .85; font-weight: 500; }
.cover .title { position: absolute; left: 16mm; top: 30mm; }
.cover .title .over { font-size: 11pt; font-weight: 600; opacity: .9; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
.cover .title h1 { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-weight: 400; font-size: 84pt; line-height: 1.02; margin: 2mm 0 0; letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
.cover .title h1 span { color: var(--acc2); }
.cover .title .sub { margin-top: 4mm; font-size: 13pt; font-weight: 700; display: flex; gap: 3mm; align-items: center; }
.cover .title .sub i { font-style: normal; font-weight: 500; opacity: .8; font-size: 10pt; }
.cover .band { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 64mm; background: #f2ff6b; color: var(--ink); padding: 9mm 16mm 0; }
.cover .band .who { font-size: 9.5pt; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .who b { color: #2440b3; }
.cover .band .slogan { font-family: "Black Han Sans"; font-size: 33pt; line-height: 1.1; margin-top: 2mm; }
.cover .band .feat { position: absolute; right: 16mm; top: 9mm; text-align: right; font-size: 8.2pt; line-height: 1.75; font-weight: 600; }
.cover .band .feat span { display: inline-block; background: var(--ink); color: #f2ff6b; padding: 0 2mm; margin-left: 1mm; font-size: 7.6pt; }
.cover .band .bot { position: absolute; left: 16mm; right: 16mm; bottom: 9mm; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 8.4pt; font-weight: 700; }
.cover .band .bot span { font-weight: 500; }
.memo { margin-top: 5mm; }
.memo .mh { font-family: "Archivo Black", Pretendard; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--navy); letter-spacing: .06em; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--ink); padding-bottom: .8mm; }
.memo .line { border-bottom: .5pt dashed #c3c7cf; }
table.tf { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 8.4pt; margin-bottom: 1mm; }
table.tf td { border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.2mm .5mm; }
table.tf td.b { width: 12mm; text-align: right; color: var(--gray); }
.sum { font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.6pt; border-top: .5pt solid var(--rule); border-bottom: .5pt solid var(--rule); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 1.4mm; }
.pair { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; font-family: Inter; font-size: 8.4pt; row-gap: .5mm; }
.q2 { margin-top: 3mm; }

:root { --brand: #213f93; --navy: #213f93; --tint: #eaf1fb; --tint2: #cfdcf2; --acc: #ff6a2b; --ink: #1a1d26; }
.page { padding: 19mm 16mm 15mm 14mm; }
.en { font-family: "Source Serif 4", Georgia, serif; font-size: 9.7pt; line-height: 1.6; letter-spacing: 0; }
/* header band */
.run { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 11mm; margin: 0; padding: 0 16mm 0 14mm; background: var(--tint); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; font-size: 7.6pt; color: var(--brand); }
.run .brand { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; padding: 1.2mm 2.6mm; font-size: 7.4pt; letter-spacing: .08em; }
.run .brand i { color: #ffd36b; }
.cover .run { display: none; }
/* thumb index */
.thumb { position: absolute; right: 0; width: 7.5mm; height: 27mm; background: var(--tint2); color: var(--brand); border-radius: 2mm 0 0 2mm; writing-mode: vertical-rl; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 6.6pt; letter-spacing: .12em; }
.thumb.on { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; }
/* part head */
.part { border-bottom: 1.2pt solid var(--brand); padding-bottom: 2.6mm; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; align-items: center; }
.part .no, .part .no.fill { font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 21pt; line-height: 1; color: #fff; -webkit-text-stroke: 0; background: var(--brand); padding: 2.2mm 3mm 2mm; border-radius: 1.6mm; }
.part .ttl .e { color: var(--brand); font-size: 16pt; }
.part .meta .time { color: var(--acc); }
/* section chips */
h3.pt .n { background: var(--brand); border-radius: 1mm; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }
/* point boxes */
.box { border: .8pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 2.6mm; margin: 0 0 4mm; overflow: hidden; }
.box > h3.pt { margin: 0 0 2mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.8mm 3mm; }
.box > :not(h3) { margin-left: 3.5mm !important; margin-right: 3.5mm !important; }
.box > :last-child { margin-bottom: 3mm !important; }
/* 판서 빈칸 */
.blank { color: transparent; border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--acc); position: relative; min-width: 15mm; }
table.note td.v { width: 40mm; white-space: nowrap; }
table.note td.k { width: 50mm; }
.blank i { position: absolute; left: 0; top: -0.5mm; color: var(--acc); font-style: normal; font-weight: 800; font-size: 8pt; }
/* choice box */
.c { white-space: nowrap; font-weight: 600; }
.c b { display: inline-block; border: .7pt solid #8796b8; padding: 0 1.4mm; line-height: 1.35; font-weight: 600; }
.c b + b { border-left: 0; }
/* tables */
table.note th, table.grid th { color: var(--brand); border-bottom: 1pt solid var(--brand); background: var(--tint); }
table.grid td.no { color: var(--brand); }
ol.q > li::before { color: var(--brand); font-family: "Archivo Black"; content: counter(q, decimal-leading-zero); }
ol.q > li { padding-left: 8mm; }
.exwrap { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 38mm; column-gap: 5mm; }
.vside { border-left: .6pt solid var(--tint2); padding-left: 3mm; font-size: 7.8pt; line-height: 1.55; }
.vside h5 { margin: 0 0 1.5mm; font-family: "Archivo Black"; font-size: 7pt; color: var(--brand); letter-spacing: .08em; }
.vside div { margin-bottom: 1.2mm; }
.vside div span { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-weight: 600; display: block; color: var(--ink); font-size: 8.3pt; }
.score { border-top: 1.4pt solid var(--brand); }
.key h4 { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }
.memo .mh { color: var(--brand); border-bottom-color: var(--brand); }
.foot .pg { color: var(--brand); }
.tip b { background: var(--acc); }
.src { color: var(--acc); }
.cover .band .who b { color: var(--brand); }

.qc { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; column-gap: 7mm; row-gap: 1.6mm; }
.qc > div { position: relative; padding-left: 7mm; }
.qc > div > em { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; font-style: normal; font-family: "Archivo Black"; color: var(--brand); font-size: 8.4pt; }
.fillw { display: inline-block; min-width: 16mm; border-bottom: .6pt solid #8b9099; }
.abc { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-size: 8.8pt; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 6mm 1fr 1fr 1fr; row-gap: .4mm; margin-top: 1.5mm; }
.abc span.h { color: var(--gray); font-family: Pretendard; font-size: 7.8pt; }

.key .row { font-size: 7.9pt; gap: 0.3mm 3.6mm; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 7.7pt; margin: 0.3mm 0; }
.key h4 { margin: 2.2mm 0 0.8mm; }
.bogi2 { font-family: "Source Serif 4", serif; font-size: 8.8pt; text-align: center; border: .7pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 1.5mm; background: var(--tint); padding: 1.3mm 0; margin: 0 0 2mm; word-spacing: 2mm; }

table.note td { padding: 1.3mm 1.2mm; font-size: 8.3pt; }
table.note td.k { width: 40mm !important; }
table.note td.v { width: 33mm !important; white-space: normal !important; }
table.note td.en { font-size: 8.9pt; line-height: 1.45; }
.key .row { font-size: 7.6pt !important; }
.key .ls div { font-size: 7.5pt !important; }
.ta{display:none} .c b.ans{}

.run .brand { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; padding: 1.2mm 2.6mm; font-size: 7.4pt; letter-spacing: .08em; }
.run .brand i { color: #ffd36b; }
.cover .run { display: none; }

.thumb { position: absolute; right: 0; width: 7.5mm; height: 27mm; background: var(--tint2); color: var(--brand); border-radius: 2mm 0 0 2mm; writing-mode: vertical-rl; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-family: "Archivo Black", sans-serif; font-size: 6.6pt; letter-spacing: .12em; }
.thumb.on { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; }

.part .ttl .e { color: var(--brand); font-size: 16pt; }
.part .meta .time { color: var(--acc); }

h3.pt .n { background: var(--brand); border-radius: 1mm; }
h3.pt .n.o { background: var(--acc); }

.box { border: .8pt solid var(--tint2); border-radius: 2.6mm; margin: 0 0 4mm; overflow: hidden; }

table.note td.v { width: 40mm; white-space: nowrap; }

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

동사의 수는 동사 바로 앞 명사가 아니라 진짜 주어가 정한다.

01명사 주어 — 수식어는 괄호로 지운다

수식어(전치사구·분사구·관계사절)는 괄호로 묶어 지우고, 남은 머리 명사에 수를 맞춘다.

동사를 먼저 찾고 → 왼쪽으로 가며 꾸밈말을 ( )로 → 남은 맨 앞 명사가 진짜 주어.

[The research] (on teenagers’ sleeping habits) (in big cities) shows a clear link with stress.[ ] 진짜 주어 · ( ) 지울 수식어 · 밑줄 동사
The books on the top shelf of the school library were donated by local writers and several generous donors last year.
The students chosen to represent our school at the national science contest practice every day after class to improve their reasoning skills.
동사 바로 앞의 library · contest에 맞추면 틀린다.

02동명사구 · to부정사구 · 명사절 주어 = 단수

-ing · To · That · What · Whether · How로 시작하는 주어 덩어리는 「~하는 것」 하나 → 단수 동사.

주어 모양해석동사
Getting ~ / To learn ~~하는 것은단수
That / What / Whether / How + S + V~라는 것 / ~하는 것 / ~인지 / ~하는 방식단수
Getting enough sleep before important exams is ultimately more helpful than studying all night.
What the survey results clearly show is that students need more time for rest.
덩어리 끝의 exams · results에 속지 말 것.

03주격 관계대명사 + 동사 — 선행사에 맞춘다

관계사절 안의 동사는 who · which · that 바로 앞 명사, 곧 선행사의 수에 맞춘다.

관계사절이 끝나면 문장 전체 동사는 다시 맨 앞 주어에 맞춘다 — 동사 두 개를 따로 판단.

Teenagers who spend more than three hours a day on their phones often feel tired and have trouble maintaining their concentration during class the next day.
The scientist who leads the research team at the university has won several awards for her research on ocean pollution.
one of the students who … 의 선행사는 the students(복수).

Sociologists argue that our perception and usage of time ① are not just basic properties of nature, like a clock ② ticking away in the background, nor are they simply psychological phenomena of individual experience. Instead, how we perceive and understand time ③ are to a large degree shaped by tradition and cultural norms. Eviatar Zerubavel’s work, The Seven Day Circle, demonstrates how the week, a fundamental unit of time, is a social invention that ④ varies across cultures, ⑤ influencing how people structure their activities and rhythms of life. Why do we consider a nine-to-five job routine? … Why do we usually pay our bills at the end of the month? … These numbers and patterns aren’t really dictated by nature or any essential human characteristic, but are rather social creations that we internalize and come to accept as “normal.”

We might not think of ourselves as global citizens yet, but it’s both necessary and possible to do so. Some people are skeptical about the idea of global citizenship, but for most of human history, people didn’t think of themselves as citizens of nation-states. After all, for most of human history, nation-states didn’t exist. The rise of nation-states over the last few centuries has led people to add state citizenship to other identities, such as family, people group, or religion. Given the connections between people around the world and the common challenges we face, we need to layer global citizenship on to these other identities. This doesn’t mean that global citizenship replaces these other identities. There’s not a single story about our identities. Instead, it’s precisely because we have obligations to our families, those in our community, and those around the world.

Sociologists argue that our perception and usage of time are not just basic properties of nature, like a clock ticking away in the background, nor are they simply psychological phenomena of individual experience. Instead, how we perceive and understand time is to a large degree shaped by tradition and cultural norms. Eviatar Zerubavel’s work, The Seven Day Circle: The History and Meaning of the Week, demonstrates how the week, a fundamental unit of time, is a social invention that varies across cultures, influencing how people structure their activities and rhythms of life. Why do we consider a nine-to-five job routine? Why don’t many of us work on the weekends? Why do we usually pay our bills at the end of the month? Why is the retirement age sixty-five? These numbers and patterns aren’t really dictated by nature or any essential human characteristic, but are rather social creations that we internalize and come to accept as “normal.”

Unfortunately, sometimes the idea of a goal is disconnected from the daily reality of what it will take to achieve it. We fall in love with the idea of a goal, pushing out of mind how different our day-to-day will need to be for us to make it happen. Paul Farmer was an American medical anthropologist and physician. He was born in 1959 in Massachusetts and grew up with an early awareness of social inequality. During his time at Duke University, he lived in Paris for half a year and became fluent in French, which benefited him in his future work in Haiti. After graduating from Duke University, he began volunteer work at a hospital in Cangé, Haiti. He later returned to the United States and earned both a master’s degree and a PhD in medical anthropology at Harvard University. In 1987, he co-founded Partners In Health, an organization that works in countries like Haiti, Rwanda, and Peru to provide medical treatment and strengthen public health systems. Throughout his life, he wrote more than ten books and over a hundred academic papers. He received many major awards during his career, and after his death, he was also honored with the WHO Director-General’s Global Health Leaders Award for his lifelong work to improve health for the poor.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

강조하고 싶은 말이 문장 앞으로 나오면 주어와 동사의 자리가 바뀐다.

01부정어(구) 도치 — Never · Little · Seldom · Hardly · Rarely

핵심부정어가 문장 맨 앞에 오면 (조)동사 + 주어 순서. 일반동사는 do · does · did + 주어 + 동사원형.

She has never told a lie → Never has she told a lie
도치Never has our small school hosted so many visitors from other cities for a single event.
도치Little did the scientists know that their small discovery would change the whole industry.

주의Never she has told (×) — 부정어 뒤가 「주어 + 동사」 그대로면 틀린다.

02Only + 부사(구·절) 도치

핵심Only then / Only after ~ / Only when ~ 이 앞에 오면 그 뒤 주절이 「조동사 + 주어」로 뒤집힌다.

도치Only after the coach changed the plan did the team start to win games.
도치Only then did I realize that I had left my wallet on the bus.

학평·수능Only after 「절」 안은 그대로, 뒤의 주절만 도치 — changed the plan did the team

03Not until ~ / Hardly ~ when

핵심Not until A + 조동사 + 주어 + 동사 「A하고 나서야 비로소 ~」. Hardly had S p.p. when ~ 「~하자마자」.

He didn’t realize it until he lost his phone → Not until he lost his phone did he realize it
도치Not until he lost his phone did he realize how much time he spent online.
도치Hardly had I closed my eyes when the fire alarm in the building began to ring.

주의Not until 뒤에는 절이 와도 도치는 「주절」에서 — until he lost did he (○)

04장소 · 방향 부사구 도치 — 동사 + 주어

핵심장소·방향 부사구가 앞에 오면 동사 + 주어. 조동사 do를 쓰지 않고 동사를 그대로 앞으로. 동사의 수는 뒤의 주어에 맞춘다.

보통 어순도치

주의주어가 대명사면 도치하지 않는다: Here it comes (○) / Here comes it (×)

05보어 도치 — So + 형용사 + 동사 + 주어

핵심보어(형용사)가 앞으로 나오면 동사 + 주어. So ~ that 구문이 자주 쓰인다.

학평·수능So 형용사 + 동사 + 주어 — 동사의 수는 뒤 주어(the children → were)

06So / Neither / Nor + 동사 + 주어 — 「~도 그렇다」

핵심긍정에 맞장구는 so, 부정에 맞장구는 neither · nor. 동사는 앞 문장의 동사 종류·시제를 따른다.

앞 문장맞장구
be동사 · 조동사… and so is he / neither can we
일반동사 현재 · 과거… and so does she / neither did they
긍정My brother enjoys hiking in the mountains on weekends, and so does my father.
부정The students didn’t understand the new rule, and neither did their parents.

주의neither 뒤에 not을 또 쓰지 않는다: neither didn’t they (×)

07There / Here + 동사 + 주어

핵심There · Here가 앞에 오면 동사 + 주어. 동사의 수는 동사 뒤의 명사가 정한다.

복수There are several reasons why teenagers should get enough sleep every night.

핵심such + a(n) + 형용사 + 명사 / so + 형용사 + a(n) + 명사 / 형용사 + enough

Suppose you have been working on the solution to a challenging technological problem for many years. Let’s also suppose that you have been paying attention to ① whatever else you have encountered that might be related to the problem. In that case, chances are that creative solutions to the problem could suddenly pop up in your mind when you ② are relaxed. Such “eureka moments” (when great insights lead to discovery or invention) often ③ take place at unexpected times. To enhance spontaneous creativity, therefore, one must pay attention to the things that could potentially ④ leads to valuable outcomes. This does not mean that you must narrow down your interest to one specific topic. On the contrary, breadth of experience is the key to creativity. A classical ideal of truth and knowledge is the concept of a market for ideas: as thinking individuals, we encounter competing ideas, we evaluate them for their best fit to reality, and then let the best and brightest facts form the basis of our beliefs. That would be the scientist’s way, in theory at least. But in practice, most of the time we are in a market for justifications. By treating language with greater respect, we can achieve more than simple self-defense.

3 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?①22번

Suppose you have been working on the solution to a challenging technological problem for many years. Let’s also suppose that you have been paying attention to whatever else you have encountered that might be related to the problem. In that case, chances are that creative solutions to the problem could suddenly pop up in your mind when you are relaxed. Such “eureka moments” (when great insights lead to discovery or invention) often take place at unexpected times. To enhance spontaneous creativity, therefore, one must pay attention to the things that could potentially lead to valuable outcomes. This does not mean that you must narrow down your interest to one specific topic. On the contrary, breadth of experience is the key to creativity. If your experience is limited to a narrow range of topics, then the scope of your imagination will likewise be narrow, which would be harmful to creativity.

Shame is about who we are, and guilt is about our behaviors. We feel guilty when we hold up something we’ve done or failed to do against the kind of person we want to be. It’s an uncomfortable feeling, but one that’s helpful. When we apologize for something we’ve done, make amends to others, or change a behavior that we don’t feel good about, guilt is most often the motivator. Guilt is just as powerful as shame, but its effect is often positive while shame often is destructive. When we see people apologize, make amends, or replace negative behaviors with more positive ones, guilt is often the motivator, not shame. In fact, in my research, I found that shame corrodes the part of us that believes we can change and do better.

5 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?②24번

Let’s look at what is occurring in your brain when scrolling on social media, a quick dopamine activity. You open your social media apps and immediately you notice you feel really good, your dopamine levels increase incredibly fast and pleasure is experienced in your brain. The challenge this creates is as with everything in our universe: as the laws of physics explain, ‘what goes up, must come down’. Your brain and body are always seeking something called ‘homeostasis’, which simply means balance. With this in mind, when dopamine levels increase incredibly fast when scrolling social media, the brain then thinks, ‘Wow, how are my dopamine levels so high?’ In order to achieve homeostasis, or balance, the dopamine then has to quickly drop an equal amount below your baseline level in order to rebalance, making you feel even worse than before you started scrolling.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

01한 절에 본동사는 하나

핵심접속사 없이 본동사는 하나. 나머지 동사 모양(to-v · -ing · p.p.)은 준동사다.

동사The students finished the science project early and presented it to the whole class on Friday.
준동사The scientist paused for a moment to consider the unexpected results of the long experiment.

주의and · but · or로 이은 동사는 앞 동사와 모양을 맞춘다(병렬): finished … and presented

02동사 수 = 접속사 · 관계사 수 + 1

핵심접속사 · 관계사가 하나 있으면 동사는 둘. 동사 수가 남으면 하나는 준동사로 바꾼다.

The book that my teacher recommended → is sold out → that 1개 + 1 = 동사 2개
관계사The book that my teacher recommended last week is now sold out in most bookstores.
접속사Many researchers believe that spending time outdoors lowers stress in young children.

학평·수능29번은 문장 속 접속사 · 관계사 수를 세면 동사 자리가 바로 보인다.

핵심동사원형은 주어가 될 수 없다. -ing 또는 to-v로 쓰고 동사는 단수.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

to부정사는 「to + 동사원형」, 동명사는 「동사원형 + -ing」. 둘 다 동사에서 나왔지만 문장에서는 명사 · 형용사 · 부사로 일한다.

01to부정사 — 명사 역할 (주어 · 보어 · 목적어)

「~하는 것, ~하기」. 주어가 길면 가주어 It ~ to-v로 뒤로 보내고, to부정사 주어는 단수 동사.

가주어It is important to get enough sleep before an exam because tired students make more careless mistakes.
목적어Many students hope to join the science club, but only twenty members can be accepted this year.

주의To learn new words every day are (×) → is (○)

02to부정사 — 형용사 역할 (명사 뒤에서 꾸밈)

「~할 (명사)」. 명사 뒤에서 꾸미고, 동사가 자동사면 전치사까지 붙인다: a chair to sit on.

수식Our school library offers students a quiet place to study after classes and on weekends.
전치사The new students needed someone to talk with during their first week at the large high school.

주의a friend to play (×) → a friend to play with (○)

03to부정사 — 부사 역할 (목적 · 감정의 원인 · 판단 · 결과)

동사 · 형용사 · 문장 전체를 꾸민다. 가장 많이 나오는 것은 목적 「~하기 위해」.

쓰임해석예
목적~하기 위해saved money to buy a bike
감정의 원인~해서glad to see you
판단의 근거~하다니foolish to believe it
결과(결국) ~하다grew up to be a doctor
목적Many volunteers gathered at the beach early in the morning to collect plastic waste left by tourists.
감정The students were surprised to learn that the old tree in the schoolyard was over three hundred years old.

학평·수능문장 앞 「To-v ~, 주절」은 「~하기 위해」. 동사원형으로 시작하게 바꾼 오답이 단골.

04동명사 — 명사 역할 (주어 · 목적어 · 보어 · 전치사의 목적어)

「~하는 것」. 주어면 단수 동사, 전치사 뒤에는 to-v가 아니라 동명사.

주어Keeping a diary in English every night has helped many students improve their writing skills.
전치사She is interested in learning how robots can help elderly people who live alone in the countryside.

주의Thank you for help me (×) → for helping me (○)

05to부정사만 목적어로 — 앞으로 할 일

바람 · 계획 · 결심처럼 미래를 향한 동사는 to-v를 목적어로 쓴다.

to-v만 쓰는 동사
want · hope · wish · plan · decide · expect · agree · refuse · promise · manage · afford · learn
decideThe team finally decided to postpone the outdoor concert because of the heavy rain forecast for Saturday.
manageAfter weeks of practice, the hesitant student managed to give a confident speech in front of the whole school.

학평·수능decide · plan · refuse · agree 뒤 -ing는 단골 오답.

06동명사만 목적어로 — 이미 하는 일 · 경험

즐기기 · 피하기 · 끝내기처럼 이미 하고 있거나 해 본 일을 나타내는 동사는 -ing를 목적어로 쓴다.

-ing만 쓰는 동사
enjoy · avoid · mind · finish · keep · consider · suggest · deny · give up · put off · practice · quit
avoidMany teenagers avoid asking questions in class because they are afraid of making mistakes in front of others.
suggestThe doctor suggested walking for thirty minutes every day instead of taking the elevator at work.

주의suggest to go (×) → suggest going (○)

07둘 다 쓰지만 뜻이 다른 동사

to-v는 앞으로 할 일, -ing는 이미 한 일. stop · try는 뜻 자체가 달라진다.

동사+ to-v+ -ing
remember · forget~할 것을~한 것을
regret~하게 되어 유감이다~한 것을 후회하다
stop~하기 위해 멈추다~하는 것을 그만두다
try~하려고 노력하다시험 삼아 ~해 보다
과거I still remember visiting the national museum with my grandfather when I was in elementary school.
목적The hikers stopped to take pictures of the beautiful lake surrounded by tall mountains and colorful autumn trees.

학평·수능remember · forget 뒤는 next week(미래) / last year(과거) 같은 단서로 판단.

덩어리째 외운다. 특히 spend · have difficulty 뒤 -ing, too ~ to-v.

표현뜻

-ingMany students have difficulty concentrating on their homework when their phones are within easy reach.

학평·수능spend time -ing / have difficulty -ing 자리에 to-v를 넣은 오답이 잦다.

For it’s not the same river and he’s not the same man.” To that, Cratylus, a student of Heraclitus, added that we are not mere passive observers. When you step in a river, you change it. Nothing is static. Even microscopic changes add up over time.

Do you always study in the same spot? Don’t. If you study in different places, that helps create variety, and that rich experience can reinforce what you are learning. When several college students told us they did school work in different places rather than in some favorite nook, that habit reflected the research on learning. Numerous experiments have found that if learners simply  , they are more likely to recall the material. In one of the first such trials, two different groups studied a list of words. Some students returned to the same room twice while their counterparts spent the same amount of time divided between two locations. When asked to recall as many words on the list as possible, those who had moved around did far better. One of the most fascinating and empowering insights in Stoic philosophy is that our emotions are not random; they arise from our  . This may sound surprising, especially if you’ve ever felt overwhelmed by anger, fear, or sadness. But the Stoics taught that emotions aren’t just automatic reactions. They’re shaped by how we interpret events. Here’s how it works: something happens, you interpret what it means, and that interpretation triggers an emotional response. For example: If someone criticizes you, you may feel angry not due to the words themselves but because you perceive the comment as unfair or threatening. If you lose a job, you might feel devastated not simply because of the job loss but because you believe it defines your worth or future. Change the judgment, and you change the emotion. This doesn’t mean suppressing how you feel; it means examining the story you tell yourself and choosing one that serves you better.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

준동사(to부정사 · 동명사 · 분사)에도 행위자 · 시간 · 태가 있다. 의미상 주어 · 완료형 · 수동형을 모양으로 익힌다.

01to부정사의 의미상 주어 — for + 목적격

핵심to부정사의 행위자가 문장 주어와 다르면 to 앞에 for + 목적격을 쓴다. 가주어 It 구문 · too ~ to · enough to에서 자주 나온다.

It is important + for teenagers + to get enough sleep
forIt is important for teenagers to get at least eight hours of sleep during the exam period.
tooThe last problem on the test was too challenging for most students to solve in time.

주의의미상 주어가 일반 사람(we · people)이면 for ~를 생략한다.

02사람의 성격 형용사 — of + 목적격

핵심kind · nice · wise · careless · foolish · rude · generous처럼 사람의 성격을 말하는 형용사 뒤에는 of + 목적격.

형용사의미상 주어
important · easy · hard · necessary · naturalfor + 목적격 (일에 대한 판단)
kind · nice · wise · careless · foolish · rude · generousof + 목적격 (사람에 대한 판단)
ofIt was kind of my classmate to lend me her notes when I missed school because of a cold.
ofIt was careless of my brother to forget his laptop and other belongings on the bus after the long school trip.

학평·수능「It is + 형용사 + [for / of] + 목적격 + to-v」 고르기가 단골.

03동명사의 의미상 주어 — 소유격(목적격)

핵심동명사의 행위자가 문장 주어와 다르면 동명사 앞에 소유격을 쓴다. 일상 영어에서는 목적격도 쓴다.

소유격My parents did not like my staying up late to play online games with my friends.
목적격The coach was proud of his team winning the championship after a long and difficult season.

주의주격(he · they) + -ing는 틀린다: they being late (×) → their being late (○)

04완료부정사 — to have p.p.

핵심to부정사의 일이 본동사보다 먼저 일어났으면 to have p.p.를 쓴다. seem · be said · be believed 뒤에 자주 온다.

It seems that the boy was hungry → The boy seems to have been hungry
완료The old castle on the hill seems to have stood there for more than five hundred years.
완료The writer is said to have lived in Paris for ten years before she became famous.

학평·수능seem 뒤 「to + 원형 vs to have p.p.」 — 시간 표현(yesterday · last week)이 열쇠.

05완료동명사 — having p.p.

핵심동명사의 일이 본동사보다 먼저 일어났으면 having p.p.를 쓴다.

완료He regrets having wasted so much time playing games instead of preparing for the test.
완료The student finally admitted having copied his classmate’s report and apologized to the teacher after class.

주의deny · admit · regret · be proud of 뒤에 자주 온다.

06수동부정사 — to be p.p.

핵심to부정사의 의미상 주어가 동작을 받으면 to be p.p.를 쓴다. need · want · expect 뒤에 자주 온다.

형태능동수동
to부정사to repairto be repaired
동명사repairingbeing repaired
완료to have repairedto have been repaired
수동The leftover pizza from the party needs to be stored in the refrigerator until lunch tomorrow.
수동Every student wants to be praised by their teachers after working hard on a difficult project.

학평·수능the window needs to repair (×) → the window needs to be repaired (○) — 창문이 「고쳐지는」 쪽.

07수동동명사 — being p.p. / having been p.p.

핵심동명사의 의미상 주어가 동작을 받으면 being p.p., 받은 일이 더 앞서면 having been p.p.를 쓴다.

수동Nobody likes being ignored by their friends when they share their worries about school.
완료She was proud of having been chosen as the leader of the science club last year.

주의전치사 뒤 수동: of being p.p. — of be p.p. (×)

01등위접속사 and · but · or — 같은 모양끼리

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

관계사 = 앞 명사(선행사)를 꾸미는 절을 여는 말. 뒤 절이 완전한지 · 불완전한지가 열쇠.

01관계대명사 = 접속사 + 대명사

핵심선행사가 사람이면 who, 사물·동물이면 which, 둘 다 that. 뒤 절에는 주어나 목적어가 하나 빠져 있다.

격사람사물 · 동물둘 다
주격whowhichthat
목적격who(m)whichthat
소유격whosewhose—
사람The teacher who taught us history last year has moved to a school in another city.
사물The phone which I bought last month already has a long crack on its screen.

주의뒤 절에 빠진 성분이 없으면 관계대명사 자리가 아니다.

02주격 관계대명사 + 동사 — 수는 선행사에

핵심who · which · that 바로 뒤 동사의 수는 선행사에 맞춘다. 지난 단원 수일치와 같은 원리.

복수Students who read news articles every day tend to write better essays than other students.
단수The old bridge that connects the two villages was built about fifty years ago.

학평·수능「one of the + 복수명사 + who」 — 선행사가 복수명사라 동사도 복수.

03목적격 관계대명사는 생략할 수 있다

핵심목적격 who(m) · which · that은 생략 가능 → 「명사 + 주어 + 동사」가 바로 붙는다.

the book (that) my teacher recommended = the book my teacher recommended
생략The book my teacher recommended turned out to be the most useful one for the final exam.
생략Most of the photos we took during the school trip were lost when my phone broke.

주의주격은 생략하지 않는다. 단, 「주격 + be동사」는 함께 생략할 수 있다.

We go out in the world every day and make decisions about what is safe or not and what is appropriate or not. It is what psychologist Joseph LeDoux has suggested is an unconscious “danger detector” that determines whether or not something or someone is safe before we can even begin to consciously make a determination. When the object, animal, or person is assessed to be dangerous, a fear response, which has been called “fight or flight,” occurs. On a conscious level we may correct a mistake in this “danger detector” when we notice it, but often, of course, we simply begin to generate reasons for why it was accurate in the first place. We are generally convinced that our decisions are “rational,” but in reality, most human decisions are made emotionally, and then we collect or generate the facts to justify these decisions. From an evolutionary perspective, self-esteem has developed as a monitoring mechanism for the quality of our relationships. The system monitors other people’s reactions to our behaviors and sends an alarm that alerts us to any possible changes in our inclusion status. The monitoring system generally operates nonconsciously until it detects that our relational value is falling or low. When the alarm bell rings, the threat to our social bonds is pushed into conscious awareness and we evaluate the situation. Am I being accepted or am I being pushed out? Do I need to adjust my behaviors to fix the relationship? With such a high value for survival closely tied with relationships, it makes sense that the way we mobilize our internal resources around relationships would be highly networked in our brain and body. It also makes sense that we would develop specific mechanisms to attend to minimizing rejection and enhancing acceptance. The continuous scanning is normal, a part of being human. We all have an interpersonal process of searching for cues from the environment to assess our value in the social structure.

종류대표 단어
물질 · 추상information · advice · evidence · knowledge · progress · homework
집합적 사물furniture · equipment · baggage · luggage · clothing · machinery
불가산Reading newspapers every morning helps students gain a lot of knowledge about the world around them.
단수All of my luggage was checked by a security officer at the airport before I got on the plane.

02수량 형용사 — few / little, many / much

핵심셀 수 있는 복수명사 앞 (a) few · many, 셀 수 없는 명사 앞 (a) little · much. a가 없으면 「거의 없는」.

셀 수 있는 명사셀 수 없는 명사
약간 있는a few studentsa little time
거의 없는few studentslittle time
많은many · a number ofmuch · a large amount of
fewVery few students in our class knew the answer to the last question on the test.
littleThe farmers got little rain this summer, so many of their crops dried up.

학평·수능a few / a little의 「약간 있는」과 few / little의 「거의 없는」 뜻 차이를 묻는다.

03재귀대명사 — 주어와 목적어가 같을 때

핵심주어 = 목적어면 목적어 자리에 -self / -selves. 다르면 him · them 같은 목적격.

재귀The new members of the drama club introduced themselves to the other students at the first meeting.
목적격The teacher promised that she would help them prepare for the national speech contest next month.

주의관용: by oneself 혼자서 · for oneself 스스로 · enjoy oneself 즐겁게 지내다

04대명사의 수 — 가리키는 명사에 맞춘다

핵심대명사(it / they, its / their)는 가리키는 명사의 수를 따른다. 거리가 멀어도 앞에서 찾는다.

단수The company changed its logo last year because many customers thought the old one looked boring.
복수Young children learn new words quickly when they hear them again and again in daily conversation.

The role of ‘slang’ in popular culture has (a) fundamentally changed because of the internet. Since the emergence of Standard English, the rule makers of language have been in charge, and their prescriptive norms about a ‘correct’ version of the English language have (b) opened up our channels of communication. If you wanted your voice to be heard by the public, you had to work within their limits, conforming to the strict expectations of either print or broadcast media. Social media completely (c) broke that barrier. The playing field is now level, and public access is democratized. Anybody and everybody can become a public figure on the new communicative platforms, meaning that nobody’s left to (d) enforce the old rules. TV presenters and journalists might not have been able to use slang, but content creators can. We regularly use words like ‘function’ and ‘side-eye,’ and our influence both legitimizes these terms and gives them a large platform to spread quicker than they could have before. Content creators also come from a (e) greater variety of backgrounds than people working in traditional media. This means that slang can more naturally go beyond the economic and social barriers that once limited its growth. The loose social networks that previously connected us geographically are simply stronger online, and memes are now transmitted at rapid pace.

Patterns such as infinite scroll, autoplaying videos, or requiring an account just to make a purchase all (a) interfere with the user’s control over their own experience. From a sustainability perspective, many of these patterns encourage (b) overconsumption of data and attention. Infinite scroll keeps loading new content whether the user wants it or not, (c) reducing data usage and device processing. Autoplay forces media to load and play even for people who may never watch it. These choices consume more energy on both the user’s device and the servers delivering the content. Take the decision by a popular music streaming platform to replace static album artwork with short video loops by default. This change significantly increases data usage and battery consumption, while the option to disable it is (d) buried deep in the settings. As a result, most users consume more resources unless they actively search for a way to opt out. It is important to acknowledge that web design always nudges behavior in some way. Showing consequences and highlighting options are all forms of influence. The ethical line is not whether nudging exists, but whether it is transparent, reversible, and aligned with the user’s interests. In many cases, the most responsible approach is to make the (e) lower-impact option the default, while keeping alternatives clearly available. Defaults are powerful, and when chosen carefully, they can reduce environmental impact without removing user agency.

* default: 기본값 ** nudge: 유도하다 *** transparent: 투명한

01원급 비교 — as ~ as

「A as 원급 as B」는 A와 B가 같은 정도. 부정은 not as(so) ~ as, 배수는 배수사 + as ~ as.

형태뜻
as 원급 as~만큼 …한
not as(so) 원급 as~만큼 …하지 않은
twice · three times as 원급 as~의 두(세) 배만큼 …한
as 원급 as possible가능한 한 …
원급The new library is as big as the old one, but it is much brighter and quieter for students to study in.
배수My older brother reads twice as many books as I do during the summer vacation every year.

주의as와 as 사이에는 원급만: as more interesting as (×)

02비교급 + than — 비교 대상을 맞춘다

비교하는 두 대상은 같은 종류여야 한다. 반복되는 명사는 that(단수) / those(복수)로 받는다.

thatThe population density of Seoul is much higher than that of any other city in the country.
thoseThe prices of fresh vegetables this winter are higher than those of last winter because a long cold spell damaged the crops in several provinces.

학평·수능than 뒤 that / those 고르기 — 앞 명사의 수를 확인한다.

03비교급 강조 — 「훨씬」

비교급 앞 「훨씬」은 much · even · far · still · a lot. very는 원급만 꾸민다.

muchReading paper books before bed is much better for your sleep than looking at a bright phone screen.
evenThe new eco-friendly electric buses are even quieter than the old ones that the city used for twenty years.

주의very more (×) · very better (×)

04the 비교급, the 비교급 — ~할수록 더 …하다

the 비교급 + S + V, the 비교급 + S + V. 「비교급 and 비교급」은 「점점 더 ~」.

The more you practice → the more confident you become
the 비교급The more carefully you read the instructions, the fewer mistakes you will make during the experiment.
점점As the city grew, the traffic on the main roads became worse and worse every single year.

학평·수능the 비교급 뒤 어순(the more carefully you read)과 형용사/부사 자리를 묻는다.

What is the Capabilities Approach (CA), and why would lawyers passionate about animal justice care about it? It is easy to say what it is not. The CA does not rank animals by likeness to humans or seek special privileges for those considered most “like us,” as do some other popular theoretical approaches. The CA has concern for the finch and the pig as much as the whale and the elephant. Just as humans seek to be able to enjoy the characteristic goods of a human life, so a finch seeks a finch’s life and the whale a whale’s life. We should extend ourselves and learn, not lazily picture animals as lesser humans, seeking a life sort of like our own. Kivetz, Urminsky, and Zheng partnered with a café to test the motivating effect of illusory progress in an experiment. Customers received a reward card that offered one free coffee after they’d bought ten. While half of the customers received a card with ten open slots, the other half got a card with twelve open slots. Yet the twelve-slot card had two preexisting “bonus” stamps, so, strictly speaking, these were identical reward programs. Every customer who got a card needed to make ten coffee purchases (and collect ten stamps) to get their free coffee. But the appeal of the free stamps was high. People who thought they’d gotten a head start came back to the café more often, filling in their reward card more quickly than the others. When the card came with two out of twelve slots already filled, it felt to customers like they were already 16 percent finished with the goal before they’d even started. Believing they were closer to the reward, they were more motivated to reach the finish line.

BASIC어법 기본 다지기 ①

조동사는 말하는 사람의 확신 · 후회 · 의무를, 가정법은 사실과 반대인 상상을 나타낸다.

01추측의 조동사 — must · may · can’t

핵심강한 추측 must(~임에 틀림없다), 약한 추측 may / might(~일지도 모른다), 강한 부정 추측 can’t(~일 리 없다).

mustThe lights in the science lab are still on, so someone must be working on a research proposal tonight.
can’tShe can’t be the author of the report, because she was abroad during the entire project.

주의「~일 리 없다」는 mustn’t가 아니라 can’t. mustn’t는 「~하면 안 된다」(금지).

02조동사 + have p.p. — 과거에 대한 추측 · 후회

핵심지나간 일을 지금 추측하거나 후회할 때는 조동사 뒤에 have p.p.를 쓴다.

형태뜻
must have p.p.~했음에 틀림없다
may(might) have p.p.~했을지도 모른다
can’t have p.p.~했을 리 없다
should have p.p.~했어야 했는데 (안 했다)
need not have p.p.~할 필요가 없었는데 (했다)
추측The ground is completely wet, so it must have rained heavily during the night while we slept.
후회You should have checked the weather forecast before planning the outdoor event for the students.

학평·수능yesterday · last night처럼 과거 표현이 있으면 「조동사 + 동사원형」이 아니라 「조동사 + have p.p.」

03주장 · 요구 · 제안 + that + S + (should) 동사원형

핵심insist · demand · suggest · recommend · order · require 뒤 that절이 「해야 한다」는 내용이면 (should) 동사원형.

제안The doctor recommended that the patient get more rest before returning to his usual schedule.
요구The safety rules require that every visitor to the laboratory wear safety glasses at all times.

주의that절이 「사실」이면 시제 일치: The evidence suggests that he was at home that night.

04used to · would · be used to -ing

핵심과거의 습관·상태는 used to(상태 O), 과거의 반복 동작은 would(상태 X), 「~에 익숙하다」는 be used to -ing.

05had better · would rather · may as well

핵심뒤에는 모두 동사원형. 부정은 had better not · would rather not.

충고You had better not leave your bag on the bus seat if you want to keep it safe.
선택I would rather stay home and study than go to a crowded concert on a rainy night.

주의had not better (×) → had better not (○) / would rather A than B에서 A·B는 같은 동사원형.

06가정법 과거 — 지금 사실과 반대

핵심If + S + 과거형(be는 were), S + would / could + 동사원형. 해석은 「(지금) ~라면 …할 텐데」.

현재If my phone worked properly, I could call my parents and tell them where I am now.
wereIf she were the class president, she could change the rules about using phones at lunch.

If she had known, …Had she known, …

과제
1Whether we feel happy or sad, content or discontent, is not determined merely by each individual successive moment of life experience — a good thing happens and I'm happy, a bad thing happens and I'm sad.우리가 행복하다고 느끼는지 슬프다고 느끼는지, 만족하는지 불만족하는지는 단지 삶의 경험의 각각의 연속적인 순간에 의해서만 결정되는 것은 아니다 — 좋은 일이 일어나면 나는 행복하고, 나쁜 일이 일어나면 나는 슬프다는 식으로.
2While our experiences affect our mood, we are not blown in a completely new direction by each gust of wind.우리의 경험은 기분에 영향을 미치지만, 우리는 돌풍이 불 때마다 완전히 새로운 방향으로 날아가지는 않는다.
3There will be highs and lows, but over time, like water seeking its own level, we are pulled toward our baseline — back up after bad news and back down after good.기복은 있겠지만, 시간이 지나면서 제 수위를 찾는 물처럼 우리는 기준선으로 끌려간다 — 나쁜 소식 뒤에는 다시 올라오고 좋은 소식 뒤에는 다시 내려온다.
4The euphoria of first love fades, and so does the despair of a break-up.첫사랑의 행복감은 서서히 사라지고, 이별의 절망도 그러하다.
5This tendency is best seen with little kids and their toy joy: When they get what they've longed for, they believe they will be happy for the rest of their lives.이 경향은 어린아이들과 장난감이 주는 기쁨에서 가장 잘 드러난다. 아이들은 간절히 원하던 것을 얻으면 남은 평생 행복할 거라고 믿는다.
6And for the first few minutes of the rest of their lives, they are.그리고 남은 평생의 처음 몇 분 동안은 정말로 그렇다.
7But then the kids — like adults — adapt.하지만 그 후 아이들은 어른들처럼 적응한다.
